title: Claude Code is accidentally exposing secrets all over GitHub
gist: Apiiro found over 100,000 public GitHub repos containing Claude Code local settings files, of which about 1,100 across 63 organizations exposed real secrets. The leak stems from approved shell commands being stored verbatim in settings.local.json, and Anthropic has not yet shipped a fix.

insights.claim: Claude Code stores user-approved shell commands, including any embedded credentials, verbatim in the local .claude/settings.local.json file when the user picks 'Yes, and don't ask again'.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Agentic coding tools create new credential-leak surfaces through convenience features; security tooling demand follows.

insights.claim: The protective .gitignore entry Anthropic documents is applied globally rather than at repo level, so the settings file can be committed when a repo is cloned elsewhere or a folder later becomes a repo.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Design gaps in default protections, not only user error, drive the exposure.

insights.claim: Apiiro found over 100,000 public GitHub repos containing Claude Code local settings files, but only about 1,100 from 63 organizations held secrets such as API tokens, database passwords or private keys.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Roughly 1% hit rate shows the problem is real but bounded; scale grows with Claude Code adoption.

insights.claim: 215 of the roughly 1,100 exposed secrets were not flagged by gitleaks or TruffleHog, so standard secret scanners miss a meaningful share (about 20%) of this leakage.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Existing secret-scanning products have a coverage gap for AI-agent artifacts, an opening for new vendors.

insights.claim: Claude Code itself often commits changes to the settings file without the user's input, per Apiiro.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Autonomous commits remove the human checkpoint that would normally catch sensitive files.

insights.claim: Secrets can persist in forks of a project even after the settings file is removed from the original repository.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Remediation requires credential rotation, not just file deletion.

insights.claim: The issue was flagged in a Claude Code bug report as early as August 2025, and related reports were closed without action after 60 days of inactivity.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Slow triage of security-adjacent bugs is a reputational and enterprise-adoption risk for Anthropic.

insights.claim: Claude Code's Boris Cherny said the team is looking into prevention, argued these files should almost never be checked in, and said leaks arose when files were manually created and checked in.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Anthropic initially frames it as user error, which may not satisfy enterprise security buyers.

insights.claim: Cherny recommended auto mode, which uses classifiers to route routine permission prompts, but acknowledged it can still save sensitive commands to settings files and called that a good catch.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: The recommended workaround does not fully close the hole, so a product fix is still pending.

insights.claim: Anthropic is considering building secret scanning into Claude Code itself.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Native scanning would commoditize part of the third-party secret-scanning market.

insights.claim: AI agents are repeatedly leaking sensitive data unintentionally; Meta suspended the sharing feature on its Muse agent last month after researchers found its link URLs could be easily guessed.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: A pattern of agent-feature leaks raises regulatory and enterprise-governance scrutiny of AI agents.
